examples.en: Kind woodcutters often appear in old tales.

examples.ko: 나무꾼은 산에서 나무를 베어 장작을 팔았어요.
examples.en: The woodcutter cut trees in the mountain and sold firewood.
Do you know the story of 'The Fairy and the Woodcutter'?
The woodcutter dropped his axe into the pond.
A poor woodcutter and his wife lived deep in the mountains.
The mountain spirit showed the woodcutter a golden axe.

explain: 산에서 나무를 베어 생활하는 사람을 말하지만 요즘은 주로 옛이야기나 전래동화에서 만나요. 지금 직업으로는 보통 '벌목공'이라고 해요. '-꾼'은 어떤 일을 하는 사람을 나타내는 말끝이에요.

phrases.en: When I was little I read the story 'The Woodcutter and the Fairy'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국 전래동화 제목으로 가장 유명한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most famous use, the title of a Korean folk tale.

phrases.en: Long ago a poor woodcutter lived.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛이야기를 시작할 때 이렇게 자주 소개해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical way to introduce a character at the start of an old tale.

phrases.en: The woodcutter gathered wood in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나무를 하다'는 땔감으로 쓸 나무를 베거나 모은다는 뜻이라 나무꾼과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: '나무를 하다' means cutting or gathering wood for fuel, so it pairs naturally with 나무꾼.

explain_en: It refers to a person who makes a living cutting trees in the mountains, but today you mostly meet it in old tales and folktales. As a present-day job, people usually say '벌목공'. The ending '-꾼' marks a person who does a certain kind of work.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어리지만 말도 행동도 당차요.
examples.en: That child is young, but both her words and actions are spunky.
It was impressive to see her present in a bold voice.

examples.ko: 언니는 당차서 어디를 가도 잘 지내요.
examples.en: My older sister is gutsy, so she does well wherever she goes.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 당차게 자기 생각을 말했어요.
examples.en: The new employee spoke her mind boldly.

examples.ko: 저는 당차지 못해서 사람들 앞에 서면 떨려요.
examples.en: I'm not bold, so I tremble when I stand in front of people.

examples.ko: 당찼던 할머니는 젊을 때 혼자 가게를 여셨대요.
examples.en: I heard my spunky grandmother opened a shop on her own when she was young.

explain: 나이가 어리거나 작아 보이는 사람이 겁 없이 야무지고 씩씩하게 행동할 때 칭찬으로 많이 써요. '씩씩하다', '야무지다'와 비슷하지만 '당차다'는 용기와 자신감이 더 크게 느껴져요. 보통 '당찬 목소리', '당차게 말하다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: That child is really spirited and confident.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-n' form is used to describe a person.

phrases.example: 그 학생은 선생님 앞에서도 당차게 말했어요.
phrases.en: That student spoke confidently even in front of the teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겁 없이 자신 있게 말하는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes speaking boldly and without fear.

phrases.en: You're so young, but you're really confident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라면서 칭찬할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This tone is used to praise someone with a bit of surprise.

explain_en: It is often a compliment for a young or small-looking person who acts boldly, sensibly and with spirit. It is close to '씩씩하다' and '야무지다', but '당차다' feels more courageous and confident. Typical uses are '당찬 목소리' and '당차게 말하다'.

examples.en: The police are chasing a fugitive.

examples.ko: 영화 속 도망자는 끝까지 잡히지 않았어요.
examples.en: The fugitive in the movie was never caught.

examples.ko: 그는 도망자 신세가 되어 외국으로 갔어요.
examples.en: He became a fugitive and went abroad.
The house where the fugitive was hiding was found.
I heard the villagers gave the runaway some food.

examples.ko: 저는 도망자가 나오는 오래된 드라마를 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like old dramas with a fugitive in them.

explain: '도망자'는 잡히지 않으려고 달아나는 사람이에요. 비슷한 '탈주범'은 감옥이나 경찰에서 빠져나간 범인만 가리켜서 더 좁아요. 아이가 집을 나가면 '가출'이라고 해서 '도망자'를 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: He did something wrong and became a fugitive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잡히지 않으려고 숨어 다니는 신분이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone ends up hiding to avoid being caught.

phrases.example: 몇 년 동안 도망자 신세로 살았어요.
phrases.en: He lived as a fugitive for several years.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신세'가 붙어 불쌍하고 힘든 처지라는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: 신세 adds a feeling of a pitiful, hard situation.

phrases.en: The police caught the fugitive yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쫓다'와 달리 결과로 붙잡았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 쫓다, it means the person was actually caught.

explain_en: 도망자 is someone running away to avoid capture. 탈주범 is narrower, meaning a criminal who escaped from prison or police custody. A child who leaves home is 가출, not 도망자.

examples.ko: 우리 반 심술쟁이가 오늘은 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The grump of our class is smiling today.
The grumpy old man is actually the kindest.
If you act that spiteful, you won't have friends.
My younger sibling teases me by calling me a grump.
A mean witch appears in this cartoon.
Everyone knows who the grump is.

explain: '심술꾸러기'와 비슷하게 쓰는 말로, 심술을 잘 부리는 사람을 가볍게 놀리거나 부를 때 써요. '-쟁이'는 '욕심쟁이, 겁쟁이'처럼 그런 성격이나 버릇을 가진 사람에게 붙어요. 진짜 화가 났을 때보다는 장난스러운 말투에 어울려요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is a grump.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심술쟁이'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be swapped with '심술쟁이' with almost the same meaning.

phrases.example: 우리 집 심술쟁이 고양이가 또 컵을 떨어뜨렸어요.
phrases.en: Our grumpy cat knocked over a cup again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반려동물에게도 장난스럽게 붙여서 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be playfully used for pets.

phrases.en: Why are you acting like a grump today?
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소와 다르게 심술을 부릴 때 가볍게 물어보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light question for someone acting spiteful out of character.

explain_en: It is used much like '심술꾸러기' to lightly tease someone who often acts spiteful. '-쟁이' attaches to a person with that trait, as in '욕심쟁이' (greedy person) and '겁쟁이' (coward). It fits a playful tone better than real anger.

examples.ko: 두 친구는 십 년 만에 재회했어요.
examples.en: The two friends reunited after ten years.

examples.ko: 공항에서 가족과 재회하는 순간 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: The moment I reunited with my family at the airport, I cried.
We promised to meet again in our hometown.
We reunited after a long time and talked all night.
They say the couple who had broken up met again by chance.

examples.ko: 언젠가 그 친구와 꼭 재회하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I really want to be reunited with that friend someday.

explain: '만나다'는 어떤 만남이든 쓰지만 '재회하다'는 오래 헤어졌던 사람과 다시 만나는 순간에 써요. 드라마 줄거리에 자주 나오고, 평소 대화에서는 '다시 만나다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Everyone smiled with the joy of meeting again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랜만에 다시 만나서 느끼는 기쁨을 말해요. 글에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The joy of meeting again after a long time. Often seen in writing.

phrases.en: I got to meet my friend again after a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게 되다'를 붙이면 자연스럽게 다시 만나게 됐다는 느낌이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -게 되다 gives the feel that the meeting came about naturally.

phrases.en: I'm meeting my friend again tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재회하다'보다 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than 재회하다 in daily conversation.

explain_en: 만나다 works for any meeting, but 재회하다 is for meeting again someone you were apart from for a long time, usually with emotion. It appears often in drama plots, while '다시 만나다' is more natural in casual talk.

examples.en: That movie opens next week.
I haven't opened the gift box yet.
Please drink opened milk quickly.
It was released last year but is still popular.
If you open the packaging, you can't get a refund.
The video of opening the new album is popular.

explain: 영화가 처음 극장에 걸릴 때, 그리고 포장·봉투를 처음 뜯을 때 둘 다 써요. 영화는 '개봉하다'지만 책이나 노래는 '출간하다', '발매하다'라고 해요. 이미 뜯은 물건은 '개봉한 제품', 안 뜯은 것은 '미개봉'이에요.

phrases.en: That movie was released last week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화가 주어일 때 자주 쓰는 피동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, common when the movie is the subject.

phrases.en: I watched the movie with a friend on its opening day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화가 처음 나오는 날을 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common word for the day a movie first opens.

phrases.en: It's an unopened product, so it's brand new.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포장을 아직 뜯지 않은 물건에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for items whose packaging has not been opened.

explain_en: It covers both a movie first showing in theaters and breaking the seal on packaging. Movies are 개봉하다, but books and music use 출간하다 and 발매하다. An already opened product is '개봉한 제품', and an unopened one is '미개봉'.

dis.h: break a seal, or release a film

p.n: The passive cannot take an object marked with 를.

examples.en: One piano key is broken.
The child pressed the keys carefully.
Fingers move quickly over the keys.
There are fewer black keys than white keys.
I wiped the keys clean before playing.
These keys have a soft sound.

explain: 피아노나 오르간에서 손가락으로 누르는 하나하나의 키를 말해요. 컴퓨터 자판은 '키보드'나 '자판'이라고 하고, 건반은 악기에만 써요. '건반 악기'라고 하면 피아노 같은 악기를 한꺼번에 말해요.

phrases.en: Please press the piano keys slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손가락으로 소리를 낼 때 '누르다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 누르다 for pressing keys to make sound.

phrases.en: The piano is a typical keyboard instrument.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피아노, 오르간 같은 악기를 한꺼번에 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A group name for pianos, organs, and similar instruments.

phrases.en: The piano keys are white and black.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 악기의 건반인지 앞에 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the instrument name before it to say whose keys.

explain_en: This is each key you press on a piano or organ. A computer keyboard is a 키보드 or 자판; 건반 is only for instruments. 건반 악기 covers piano-type instruments as a group.

en: crossing the finish line; scoring a goal

examples.en: The marathon runner crossed the finish line first.
My family is waiting at the finish line.
The shot went in and it was a goal.

examples.ko: 마지막 주자가 골인하는 순간 모두 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: Everyone clapped the moment the last runner crossed the line.

examples.ko: 둘은 오랜 연애 끝에 결혼에 골인할 거예요.
examples.en: After a long courtship, the two will finally get married.
I handed water to the runner who had finished.

explain: 달리기에서는 결승선에 들어오는 것, 축구나 농구에서는 공이 골대에 들어가는 것에 써요. 축구 점수를 말할 때는 그냥 '골'을 더 많이 써요. 영어의 goal처럼 '목표'라는 뜻으로는 쓰지 않아요. 그럴 때는 '목표'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 둘은 삼 년 연애 끝에 결혼에 골인했어요.
phrases.en: finally get married
phrases.nuance_ko: 연애를 오래 한 두 사람이 마침내 결혼하게 될 때 가볍게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light, friendly way to say a couple finally got married after dating for a while.

explain_en: It means reaching the finish line in a race, or the ball going into the net in soccer or basketball. For a soccer score, people usually just say '골'. It does not mean 'goal' as in an aim; for that, use '목표'.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에 베토벤 교향곡을 들으러 가요.
examples.en: Tonight I'm going to hear a Beethoven symphony.

examples.ko: 이 교향곡은 연주 시간이 한 시간쯤 돼요.
examples.en: This symphony takes about an hour to perform.

examples.ko: 교향곡 연주회에는 악기가 아주 많이 필요해요.
examples.en: A symphony concert needs a great many instruments.

examples.ko: 그는 어렸을 때부터 교향곡을 작곡하고 싶어 했어요.
examples.en: He had wanted to compose a symphony since he was a child.
The symphony I like is 'Fate'.
When the fourth movement of the symphony ended, people applauded.

explain: 오케스트라가 연주하는 여러 악장으로 된 큰 곡이에요. 한두 악기로 연주하는 '소나타', 한 악기가 중심인 '협주곡'과 구분해서 써요. '제5번 교향곡'처럼 번호를 붙여 부르는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: The orchestra plays a symphony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연주하는 모습을 말할 때 쓰는 기본 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic verb phrase for performing a symphony.

phrases.en: I like Beethoven's Symphony No. 5.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교향곡은 번호를 붙여 부르는 일이 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Symphonies are often called by their numbers.

phrases.en: I'm going to a symphony concert this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교향곡을 들려주는 공연을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a concert where symphonies are performed.

explain_en: A large multi-movement piece for an orchestra. Keep it apart from 소나타 (for one or two players) and 협주곡 (concerto, built around a solo instrument). People often number them, like 제5번 교향곡.

examples.ko: 겨울마다 할머니가 손자에게 줄 목도리를 뜨개질하세요.
examples.en: Every winter, my grandmother knits a scarf for her grandson.
My grandmother is very skilled at knitting.
I learned knitting from my grandmother when I was little.
I saw someone knitting on the bus.
On my days off, I knit at a cafe.
When I knit, time passes quickly.

explain: '털실로 목도리를 뜨다'처럼 '뜨다'만 써도 같은 뜻이에요. 보통 '뜨개질을 하다'로 쓰고, 어떤 사람이 잘하면 '뜨개질에 능하다'라고 말해요. 바늘 하나로 뜨는 코바늘 뜨개질도 있어요.

phrases.en: I bought new knitting needles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨개질할 때 쓰는 도구를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the tool used for knitting.

phrases.en: My mom knitted me a winter scarf.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뜨다'만 써도 털실로 만든다는 뜻이고, 만드는 물건을 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '뜨다' alone means to knit, and you say what is being made.

phrases.en: I learned how to knit by watching YouTube.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 시작하는 취미를 말할 때 '배우다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 배우다 when talking about starting a new hobby.

explain_en: You can also use just '뜨다', as in '털실로 목도리를 뜨다', with the same meaning. It is commonly said as '뜨개질을 하다', and for someone skilled, '뜨개질에 능하다'. There is also crochet, done with a single hook, called '코바늘 뜨개질'.

examples.ko: 어제 경기에서 우리 팀 선수가 맹활약을 했어요.
examples.en: A player on our team had an outstanding game yesterday.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 새 영화에서 맹활약 중이에요.
examples.en: That actor is doing great work in his new movie.

examples.ko: 신입 사원의 맹활약 덕분에 일이 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the new employee's great work, the job finished quickly.
We won thanks to that player's outstanding performance.

examples.ko: 올해 신인 가수들의 맹활약이 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: The strong showing of this year's rookie singers stands out.
Despite his great play, the team lost.

explain: 스포츠 기사와 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '대활약'도 쓰지만, 평소 대화에서는 '진짜 잘했어요'처럼 쉬운 말을 더 많이 해요. 칭찬할 때 쓰고 나쁜 일에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: That player played brilliantly in the final.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맹활약'과 뜻이 거의 같아요. 뉴스나 기사에서 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 맹활약; both appear in news articles.

phrases.example: 신인 선수가 첫 경기에서 맹활약을 펼쳤어요.
phrases.en: The rookie played brilliantly in his first game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기사에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요. 크게 잘한 모습을 보여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common news-article pairing for showing an outstanding performance.

phrases.example: 그 선수의 맹활약 덕분에 우리 팀이 이겼어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to that player's brilliant play, our team won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘한 사람 덕분에 좋은 결과가 나왔다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a good result came thanks to someone's great play.

explain_en: It appears often in sports articles and the news. '대활약' is used for the same idea, but in everyday talk people more often say simple things like '진짜 잘했어요'. It is a word of praise and is not used for bad things.

examples.en: That player has a very fast serve.

examples.ko: 서브를 넣을 때 공을 높이 던지세요.
examples.en: Toss the ball high when you serve.
Today I only practiced serving.

examples.ko: 상대 팀의 서브가 계속 네트에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: The other team's serves kept hitting the net.
My weak point is the serve.
The score was decided by a single serve.

explain: 서브는 테니스, 배구, 탁구, 배드민턴에서 공이나 셔틀콕을 처음 쳐 넣는 동작이에요. 보통 '서브를 넣다'라고 말해요. 같은 영어 'serve'에서 왔지만 식당 서빙은 '서빙'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: That player serves first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서브하는 동작을 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say you serve.

phrases.en: That player has a good serve.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서브 실력을 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to judge someone's serving skill.

phrases.en: I practiced my serve today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연습할 때 명사로 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a noun with practice.

explain_en: 서브 is the opening shot in tennis, volleyball, table tennis, and badminton. The usual verb is '넣다': '서브를 넣다'. Waiting tables is a different borrowing, '서빙'.

examples.en: I played twenty questions with my friends.
Let's guess the answer by playing twenty questions.
I was bored in the car, so we played twenty questions.
In twenty questions, you can only answer yes or no.

examples.ko: 제가 생각한 동물이 뭔지 스무고개로 맞혀 보세요.
examples.en: Try to guess which animal I'm thinking of with twenty questions.
The kids begged to play twenty questions.

explain: 한 사람이 답을 정해 두고 다른 사람들이 질문해서 맞히는 놀이예요. 질문에는 '예/아니요'로만 대답해요. 보통 '스무고개를 하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I played twenty questions with the kids in the car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이를 한다고 말할 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic way to say you play the game.

phrases.en: Twenty questions needs no equipment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '놀이'를 붙여 게임 이름처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 놀이 makes it sound like the name of the game.

phrases.en: I'm bored, so let's play twenty questions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구에게 반말로 제안할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to suggest it to a friend in casual speech.

explain_en: One person picks an answer and the others guess it by asking questions, which can only be answered yes or no. You normally say '스무고개를 하다' (play twenty questions).

examples.en: The spotlight came on over the stage.
The rookie actor suddenly got the spotlight.
He avoids the spotlight and lives quietly.

examples.ko: 이번 영화로 감독이 다시 스포트라이트 속에 섰어요.
examples.en: With this film, the director stood in the spotlight again.
The singer sang under the spotlight.

examples.ko: 관심은 늘 주인공에게만 쏠리고 스포트라이트는 조연을 비추지 않아요.
examples.en: Attention always goes to the lead, and the spotlight does not shine on supporting actors.

explain: '스포트라이트'는 무대 조명이지만, 비유로 사람이나 사건에 관심이 몰리는 것을 가리킬 때도 많아요. 비슷한 '주목'은 딱딱한 글에 어울리고, '스포트라이트'는 한 사람에게 눈이 쏠리는 장면이 떠오를 때 써요. '스포트라이트를 받다', '스포트라이트를 피하다'로 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 신인 배우는 이번 드라마로 스포트라이트를 받았어요.
phrases.en: to be in the spotlight
phrases.nuance_ko: 조명 이야기가 아니라 사람들의 관심과 주목을 한꺼번에 받을 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively, not about lights: it means a person suddenly draws public attention.

explain_en: 스포트라이트 is a stage light, and it is also used figuratively for attention gathering on a person or event. 주목 is stiffer and suits formal writing, while 스포트라이트 fits when you picture all eyes on one person. Typical phrases are 스포트라이트를 받다 and 스포트라이트를 피하다.

examples.en: The child sings while tapping the xylophone.
I played the xylophone for the first time in music class.
The xylophone sounds clear and is pleasant to hear.
A xylophone is an instrument you hit with mallets.
They have xylophone lessons at kindergarten.
I played a simple children's song on the xylophone.

explain: '실로폰을 치다'처럼 '치다'를 쓰고, 막대로 두드리는 악기라 '두드리다'도 어울려요. 초등학교 음악 시간에 자주 쓰는 악기예요. 영어 xylophone의 소리를 옮긴 외래어예요.

phrases.en: I played the xylophone in class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기를 연주한다는 뜻으로 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural verb for playing this instrument.

phrases.en: The sound of the xylophone is clear and pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기의 소리를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for talking about the instrument's sound.

phrases.en: My friends and I played a children's song on the xylophone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곡을 실로폰으로 들려준다는 뜻으로 '연주하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '연주하다' to say a piece is played on the xylophone.

explain_en: Say '실로폰을 치다' with the verb '치다'; because you strike it with sticks, '두드리다' also fits. It is a common instrument in elementary music class. It is a loanword from the English 'xylophone'.
